title: Swath loadbench procedure and repeatability notes
body:
Context and intent:

This doc captures the current working procedure for our new "Swath" throughput bench (different from the old staircase/plateau harness). Core goals: produce repeatable throughput numbers across calibration runs, isolate warmup/caching effects, and capture heat/thermal side-effects that show up on multi-hour runs. This is intended to be the single-source-of-truth for engineers running end-to-end throughput comparisons between kernel changes, quantization profiles, and routing policies.

High-level approach (why "swath"):
- Instead of a single ramp/ramp-to-plateau run, we execute a series of overlapping throughput "swaths" (short plateaus at targeted occupancy points) spaced to let thermal and batch-adaptive behavior stabilize.
- Each swath targets a defined occupancy (percentage of GPU token-processing capacity) and runs long enough to reach steady batching and cache-hit patterns.
- Inter-swash transitions are used to surface hysteresis: how previous load shapes influence next steady state.

Environment prerequisites:
- Nodes provisioned with identical image build: bench-image:v2024-11-10; GPU drivers pinned (nvidia-535.86).
- CPU governor forced to performance on both loadgen and server: echo performance > /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/scaling_governor.
- Time sync: ntp/chrony running; chronyc tracking multiple servers.
- Clear OS pagecache before each run: sudo sync && sudo sh -c 'echo 3 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches'.
- Model artifacts pinned by checksum. Document the model repo hash in the run metadata.

Load generator and configuration notes:
- Primary tool: custom loadgen (bench-client) that supports: deterministic RNG seed, poisson and fixed-interarrival modes, per-request prompt profiles, and controlled client-side batching to simulate realistic small-batch microbursts.
- Fallback tools: k6 for HTTP-constrained checks, wrk2 for steady QPS sanity checks. Avoid vegeta for tokenized payloads (doesn't support streaming TTL headers we use).

Example swath schedule (canonical):
- Primer: 180s light traffic (10% occupancy) to let kernel JITs, lazy allocs finish. All primer requests use short prompt templates (1–16 tokens).
- Swath A: target occupancy 25% for 600s (collect steady-state metrics after first 120s).
- Transition: 60s drop to 5% occupancy (cooling, KV cache not fully invalidated).
- Swath B: 50% occupancy for 900s (collect after 180s).
- Transition: 120s drop to 10%.
- Swath C: 80% occupancy for 1200s (collect after 300s).
- Final cool-down: 300s idle.

Key configuration snippets (bench-client args) - paste-friendly:
--model-id gptx-medium:2024-11-01 --seed 1729 --arrival-mode poisson --target-occupancy 0.5 --swath-duration 900 --primer 180 --client-batch-limit 4 --token-limit 512 --log-level info

Repeatability hygiene (checklist to follow before every benchmark run):
- [ ] Confirm model checksum and config (quant, layernorm fallback flags).
- [ ] Reboot nodes if driver/kernel upgrades occurred since last run.
- [ ] Record bench-client seed explicitly. Use the same seed across calibration runs for exact stimulus alignment.
- [ ] Save and version bench-client binary and flags in run artifact directory.
- [ ] Ensure nothing else is running on the target GPUs (node-exclusive).
- [ ] Start background observability collectors (nvidia-smi loop, dstat, iostat, perf counters).
- [ ] Ensure Prometheus scrape interval set to 5s for bench window.

What to discard / retention windows:
- Always discard the first X seconds of a swath (X = max(120s, 15% of swath duration)). That slice contains residual priming and batch transients.
- Keep raw per-request logs for at least 30 days for regression analysis; aggregate tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 per-minute for quick comparisons.

Metrics to capture (minimum):
- Throughput: tokens/sec (per-GPU and cluster), requests/sec, effective concurrency (avg inflight requests).
- Latency: request written at the top-level (total), generation latency, tail-percentiles p50/p95/p99 (both server-side and client observed).
- GPU metrics: SM utilization, power draw, mem utilization, active allocations, temperature.
- Runtime internals: batch size distribution, KV cache hit rate, KV cache size, per-layer kernel times (if available), reservation queue length.
- Host-level: CPU steal, docker/container CPU shares, page faults, I/O stalls.

Notes on caching and primer strategies:
- Primer must exercise the same tokenization code path and similar prompt shapes; short primers are insufficient if production traffic is long prompts.
- For experiments isolating KV cache behavior, use a dedicated swath where prompts are identical prefixes (to maximize hits) and a companion swath with randomized prompts (to measure cold cache baseline).

Analysis heuristics and pass/fail rules:
- Repeatability: median tokens/sec across 3 independent canonical swath runs should be within 3% for code-level changes (e.g., kernel reorder). For env changes (driver/OS), expect higher variance; escalate if >7%.
- Regression detection: any p99 increase >20% or tokens/sec drop >5% triggers an automated regression ticket with attached raw logs.

PromQL snippets to validate live during runs (examples):
- tokens/sec (per model): rate(inference_tokens_total{model="gptx-medium"}[1m])
- p99 latency (server hist): histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))

Common failure modes observed in early experiments:
- Thermal throttling after consecutive high-occupancy swaths. Mitigation: insert longer cool-downs or throttle swath ceiling by 5–10%.
- JVM/GC pauses on embedding-service causing transient spikes; move embedding lookup to separate process/crio container in subsequent runs.
- Non-deterministic batch formation when client inter-arrival variance is high. Fix by capping client-batch-limit and using poisson with fixed seed.

Run artifact and naming convention:
- /bench-artifacts/swath/{model}/{kernel_hash}/{date}-{seed}-{run_id}/
- inside: bench-client-args.txt, env.txt (uname, driver, image), per-request-log.ndjson, aggregated.csv, prometheus-snapshot.json, nvidia-smi-csv.txt

Open questions / TODOs:
- Explore automatic swath-length estimator that picks duration until batch distribution converges within epsilon. (Rough prototype: check KL divergence of batch-size histogram every 30s.)
- Add kernel-level sampling with per-layer flamegraphs wired to the bench run for targeted perf regressions.
- Define standard long-run (6h) vs short-run (30m) protocols for release vs dev CI respectively. Decide minimal data collectors for CI short-run.

Quick run checklist (one-pager for engineers):
1) Checkout bench-harness @ PR-214; build bench-client vX.
2) Upload model artifact and confirm checksum.
3) Set nodes to exclusive GPU scheduling and performance governor.
4) Start prometheus and perf collectors.
5) Run bench-client with seed and swath schedule.
6) Wait for post-run artifact collection; run post-processing script: tools/bench/aggregate_swath.py --artifact-dir <path>.

If you run into unexplained variance, collect: per-request ndjson, nvidia-smi logs at 1s resolution, and host perf stat output for the suspect window. Attach to JIRA-RT-1027.

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally more prescriptive than older staircase docs. The goal is to make our verdicts reproducible across teams and to reduce flakiness in CI comparisons. Feedback most useful: missing observability signals, unrealistic swath durations, or contradictory primer guidance.
